name: Amos
overview: The book of Amos introduces a prophet who was originally a herdsman and gatherer of sycamore fruit from Tekoa, called by God to deliver a message concerning Israel during the reigns of Uzziah of Judah and Jeroboam of Israel. Despite not being a prophet by profession or lineage, Amos boldly prophesied judgment against Israel, warning of captivity and the death of King Jeroboam. His message was so unwelcome that Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, forbade him from prophesying at the king's sanctuary, highlighting the tension between divine truth and political power. Amos's visions and pronouncements underscore God's sovereign authority and the certainty of His judgment on unrepentant Israel.
